name: Udayagiri & Khandagiri Caves
description: Multi-tiered rock-cut sandstone caves, pillared verandahs, Emperor Kharavela's 17-line Brahmi Hathigumpha inscription, and the famous double-storey Rani Gumpha.

hotspots.title: Rani Gumpha (Queen's Cave Facade)
hotspots.description: Magnificent two-storey rock-cut monastery with biconcave barrel-vaulted cell doorways, carved guardian dvarapalas, and continuous narrative friezes.
hotspots.architectural_significance: Largest and most artistically rich cave in the complex, featuring acoustic courtyard resonance used for royal theatrical performances.

hotspots.title: Hathigumpha (Elephant Cave & Inscription)
hotspots.description: Natural cavern containing the priceless 17-line Brahmi Prakrit inscription recording the military triumphs, canal construction, and cultural achievements of King Kharavela.
hotspots.architectural_significance: Primary historical epigraphic source for 2nd-century BCE Indian history and early Kalinga maritime heritage.

hotspots.title: Ganesha Gumpha & Carved Plinths
hotspots.description: Cave featuring monolithic carved stone elephants flanking the front entrance and narrative reliefs of the legend of Udayana and Vasavadatta.
hotspots.architectural_significance: Demonstrates the fluid sculptural transitions from natural rock outcrop to refined architectural living quarters.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India & Epigraphia Indica Archives
sources.source: Inscriptions of Kharavela & Cave Architecture of Odisha
sources.attribution: Archaeological Survey of India & Odisha State Archaeology

reconstruction_notes: Dense photogrammetric point cloud and surface reconstruction of Rani Gumpha double-storey facade, Hathigumpha natural cavern, and sandstone hillside terraces.
surrounding_environment: Sandstone twin hills of Kumari Parvata, rocky outcrop pathways, and ancient banyan trees
